q1_what_did_you_play: Rapid Fire first, then Kaboom!, then Duck and Cover. The Spark bank is 3 and only covers one discounted Attack, so I spent it on the card whose printed cost is highest: Rapid Fire prints 2 and shows 0, Kaboom! prints 1 and shows 0. Playing Rapid Fire first for free banks the bigger discount and leaves both energy. Nibbit is the only enemy, so all four of Rapid Fire's random 4-damage hits land on it for 16. Kaboom! then costs its printed 1 for 7 more, total 23 damage into a 43 HP enemy, and the last energy buys Duck and Cover for 5 Block, so the telegraphed 12 lands as 7 and I end at 35 HP with Nibbit at 20.
q2_other_line_considered: Two. First, the mirrored order — Kaboom! at 0 and Rapid Fire at its printed 2 — same 23 damage but it eats both energy, leaves nothing for Duck and Cover, and I take the full 12. Strictly worse, so it was ruled out on sight. The one I actually weighed was the Slow Burn line: Slow Burn for 1 and Duck and Cover for 1, for 10 Block, 10 Burst Energy and Burst +5 off a meter sitting at 20 of 40. That takes the incoming 12 down to 2 and buys real meter progress. I rejected it because Slow Burn spends the 3 Sparks itself, so it burns the same resource that is currently worth a free Rapid Fire, and it deals zero damage into a 43 HP enemy I cannot kill this turn either way.
q3_what_it_gave_up: The Burst meter and the fuller guard. I skipped Slow Burn entirely, so I gave up 10 Burst Energy and the Burst +5, and I left the meter where it was; Slow Burn also stays in hand competing for a future turn's Spark bank rather than being cashed now. I took 7 to the face instead of 2 by settling for 5 Block instead of 10, and I spent the whole Spark bank on damage, so my Attacks are back to printed cost next turn with nothing banked.
q4_different_intent: Yes, though it takes a lot. Against this 12 the race maths is clear and 23 damage is worth 7 HP. If Nibbit had telegraphed something large enough that the extra 5 Block mattered for survival — roughly high thirties against my 42, or anything that would put me in lethal range — I would switch to Slow Burn plus Duck and Cover for 10 Block and bank the Burst instead. A defensive or block-gaining telegraph would also move me: chipping 23 into a wall that is about to gain armour is worth less than the meter, so I would take the Slow Burn line there too. A weaker attack, or a second enemy on the board, would not have changed anything — a second body only makes Rapid Fire's random split less certain, not less worth playing first.
